newsitem.title: JAPAN: Panel agrees on diet consent for choosing BOJ head.
newsitem.headline: Panel agrees on diet consent for choosing BOJ head.

text.p: An advisory committee discussing reforms of Bank of Japan regulations agreed on Friday to require parliamentary consent for appointments of central bank governor and deputy governor, a committee chairman said.
Currently, they only need to be appointed by the cabinet. If the proposal becomes law, the BOJ officials would need parliamentary consent then a cabinet appointment.

They also agreed to maintain the current system of the BOJ budget needing approval from the finance minister, Ryuichiro Tachi, chairman of the government subcommittee discussing BOJ law reforms, told a news conference.
One difference from the current system would be that the reasons for rejecting the budget must be made public.

"We decided to cope with this issue through the system of obtaining approval, taking into account the public characteristics of the organisation. We should define which areas need approval and make public the reasons if the budget is rejected," Tachi said.
The members also agreed to state explicitly in the general provisions that the BOJ's independence should be secured in a wide range of operations, Tachi said.

Asked about the bank's special low-interest loans made without collateral to banks, a Finance Ministry official who attended the meeting said that the BOJ could extend those without involving the ministry if the bank is not involved in any financial crisis and the liquidity crunch is temporary.
In case of financial crisis, the finance minister would ask the BOJ's policy-making board to extend the special loans. The board would make the final decision, the official said.
